header: L1 · The developer who uses it every day · sonnet
verdict: Mostly met: 25 of 26 round-8 items resolved as stated; one regression on gate 1 (01 1.4 still says every sbx command exits 3, against the new 01 1.5 protective-command rule), one unapplied sentence (daily editing setup) and one advisory on the lost-sandbox run block.

findings.defect: Gate 1 still says 'Every command that invokes sbx compares the live sbx version ... and exits 3 on a mismatch', while 01 1.5 now lets salvage, salvage --from-host, stop and pull print a gate 1 failure and go on.
findings.scenario: Docker Desktop updates sbx overnight. An implementer of T074 reads 1.4 and makes stop and salvage exit 3 (the old I7 E test); another reads 1.5 and lets them go on. The user either cannot save work before approving a catalog diff, or gets behaviour the gate text denies.
findings.change: In 01 1.4 say 'every command except the protective commands of 1.5' and name the exemption, or point to 1.5 after 'exits 3'. Check the I7 E list and the J9 sbx update step for the same sentence.

findings.defect: The one-sentence statement of the supported daily setup (edit and debug inside the sandbox; host clones are for reading in Restricted Mode) is not in 02 2.3 or anywhere else. SC4 declined the deferral and the deletion of dev.code-workspace, but not this sentence, which the cluster said could be applied on its own.
findings.scenario: The user opens dev.code-workspace, gets no extensions and no debugger, trusts the folder to get work done, and doctor then fails vscode-trust (I23), which blocks every run.
findings.change: Add the sentence next to the dev.code-workspace line of 2.3 and in the README outline, or record in the Status that it was declined.

findings.defect: The loss block that run prints before exiting 1 names the handoff command and J10 step 3 but not the command that creates the new sandbox (romeu run <name>), and the exit 1 has no row in the error table although 4.1 gives every error an id and a fix hint.
findings.scenario: After a lost sandbox, the user runs romeu run foo, sees a block and exit 1, and reads it as a failure that needs J10; the next run is the creating one, and only 01 1.6 says so.
findings.change: Add 'then romeu run <name> creates the new sandbox' to the fixed block, and give the exit-1 outcome a table row (an id or a named non-error outcome).
